data.body: WAVE 1 - REPRODUCIBILITY STATE. All 20 runs snapshotted via harness/judged.py: 0 unsnapshotted, 0 count mismatches, 0 drifted, 1 recorded divergence, 1 known-lost. The 1 recorded divergence is 2127-348c-PASS/CE, where the judged 16-row snapshot was recovered by verbatim title match from commit 2946e4b and frozen at runs/judged/; runs/ holds a later 22-row execution preserved as a replicate. The 1 known-lost is eb6e-f43a-PASS/CE: two CE agents were live on that run simultaneously and the judge scored a 13-row synthesis that existed on disk only between commits. Three other CE executions of that arm survive (9, 16 and 19 rows) and none is the judged set; 7 of the 13 judged rows appear nowhere. That artifact now carries a caveat naming all 13 rows. Not re-run and not re-judged, because a fresh run would produce different findings and paper over the gap. Guard added: judged.py snapshots every arm output at judging time with hash and finding-id list, refuses to replace a differing snapshot, and is wired into validate.py; CE_INSTRUCTIONS and SP_INSTRUCTIONS now require a guard check before writing. Side effect worth knowing: .gitignore excluded runs/*.traj.json, so mini trajectories were never in git - the snapshots give that arm its first history protection.
